idea.value: A contest announcement told as a chain of numbers arriving: every claim is a value that counts up on screen, so the viewer watches the stake grow rather than reading about it.

audience.value: People who already trade on-chain or use prediction markets: the film never explains leverage, long or short, or what a perpetual is, and it expects them to read a ticker card in 0.2 s.

value.device: Sender, then category, then the event, then one verb of urgency: four text states in 2.9 s on empty grounds, the last on a hard colour change.
value.description: Logo alone on paper (0-0.97 s); one small blue word replaces it (F29); a second word joins (F43); hard cut to a saturated blue field with 'is live' pushing in from 60% scale with rings expanding behind it (F63). The first frame shows no product and no promise: the eye has nothing to read but one word in a large empty frame, so each new word is an event. The colour flip at 2.10 s is the first jolt.

value.purpose: Announce: who, what, that it is happening now
value.retentionDevice: Sparse words, each replacing the last; first colour flip at 2.10 s
value.content: Logo, the product-line word alone, then with the word naming the event, then a two-word all-caps launch line

value.purpose: Name the stake and the cadence
value.retentionDevice: Counter ticks to the prize, then a bar chart climbs and swallows the frame
value.content: $45,000 to $50,000; bar chart fills to blue; 'EVERY 2 WEEKS'

value.purpose: Show breadth of what can be traded
value.retentionDevice: Dark pause, then a coin spins in and lands in a card; the card cycles assets, then pulls back to an endless row

value.purpose: Show the single action, then what it could reach
value.retentionDevice: Real-looking interface operated by itself; the button grows until it hides the interface; hard cut to a gauge racing to its maximum
value.content: Order form: amount to $100, leverage to 50x, place order; gauge $2K to $100K

value.retentionDevice: Three hard text swaps with changing scale: big, small, biggest
A profit figure running up, then the same figure seen in a ranking row labelled as the viewer, at rank 1
value.content: +$447k counter; ranking with '(You)' row pinned, then punch in

value.retentionDevice: Threshold counts up, top prize counts up with a tag wiping in, an itemised paper slip prints itself
value.content: the ranking cut-off as a number, then a five-word all-caps reward line, then the first prize as a figure, prize breakdown slip

value.retentionDevice: Countdown collapses from 13 days to zero in 1.3 s; zero is held; the title of the first round lands on the cut

value.purpose: Recap, and turn the offer into a dare
value.retentionDevice: Motion stops: after 27 s of constant movement the frames go still, so the one question reads with weight
value.content: $30K to $50K; the period as a three-word all-caps line; the closing dare, a seven-word all-caps question

value.retentionDevice: The rings from the opening return, so the film closes its own loop; then quiet end card
value.content: 'START TRADING' over rings and a line chart; product word and address; logo with legal text

payoff.value: The dare at 29.17 s, a question whether the viewer can make the ranking, is the payoff: all the numbers were building to the viewer's own place on that ranking.

callToAction.value: One verb phrase on the blue ground at 30.1-31.73 s, then the address at 31.73-33.17 s. The same two words have already appeared at 14.4-15.5 s as the rule of entry, so the action is rehearsed.

whyItWorks: No voice (speech-text.json holds no words) and at most one idea per frame, so it plays muted and needs no translation of anything but short words.

A number counting up is a story in under a second: it has a beginning, tension and an arrival. The film uses this at least seven times (spans in techniques.json), so its grammar is learned by the second use.
Three grounds (saturated blue, near-white, black) changed by hard cut mean a jolt of contrast every 0.95 s at the median, without any effect being applied.
The ranking row labelled for the viewer casts them as the winner before the film tells them what winning pays.
Stopping the motion at 27-30 s after constant drift makes the closing question the loudest moment visually, because nothing else is moving.
